My understanding is that Lean supports deprecating options now. However, trying to use this in mathlib does not turn up any warnings. Here is how I checked:

import Mathlib.Tactic.Linter.Whitespace

-- check: linter.style.commandStart is deprecated in favour of linter.style.whitespace

-- issue: setting the deprecated option does not yield any warning
set_option linter.style.commandStart true
set_option linter.style.whitespace true

The relevant code in file#Mathlib.Tactic.Linter.Whitespace is

public register_option linter.style.whitespace : Bool := {
  defValue := false
  descr := "enable the whitespace linter"
}

/-- Deprecated in favour of `linter.style.whitespace` -/
@[deprecated linter.style.whitespace (since := "2026-01-07")]
public register_option linter.style.commandStart : Bool := {
  defValue := false
  descr := "deprecated: use the `linter.style.whitespace` option instead"
}

Any ideas what's going wrong here?

Deprecating options works like this:

/-- Deprecated in favour of `linter.style.whitespace` -/
register_option linter.style.commandStart : Bool := {
  defValue := false
  descr := "deprecated: use the `linter.style.whitespace` option instead"
  deprecation? := some { since := "2026-01-07", text? := "use the `linter.style.whitespace` option instead" }
}

I don't recall off the top of my head why the syntax is different here; I'm sure @Wojciech Różowski will know.
Ah, so the mathlib syntax was wrong all the time. That explains it, thanks!
(I also find it confusing that the other syntax silently does nothing without raising a warning.)

Ideally we should also get a deprecation message when referring to the option in meta code! :) It seems like deprecation? is not enough to provide this, and currently we need both deprecation? and @[deprecated].

I wonder if this means that register_option should automatically add a (linter) deprecation entry based on the value of deprecation?? It would be nice to have a single interface for deprecation.

(Also maybe OptionDeprecations should also allow us to refer to another option, like @[deprecated] does, but that's a different issue.)

Hi folks,

I have just queued lean4#14478 to be merged, that changes the way we deprecate user defined options (via. register_option). Basically, you should use the deprecated attribute. Under the hood we populate the deprecation? field using the information from the attribute. If deprecation? field is provided, users are warned and asked to use deprecated attribute. Thanks to that we can have warnings in meta code as well. Also, OptionDeprecation now allows us to refer to other name.

TLDR: I implemented all of @Thomas Murrills suggestions! Thanks!
That's awesome! :D As odd as it sounds, I'm excited to deprecate some options! :smile:
